question: Should Browser CLI `--fields-file` become a documented 1 MiB-limited input contract, even when existing users may have larger valid JSON field files?
rationale: The implementation mechanism is bounded and evidenced, but choosing a new unconditional CLI input limit changes accepted user input and cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical repair.

options.title: Adopt and document the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Approve the cap as the supported Browser CLI boundary and add the user-facing contract and focused boundary coverage before merge.

options.title: Preserve the current accepted-input contract
options.body: Do not merge the unconditional cap until the owner chooses a compatible resource-control design for large valid files.

recommendation.title: Adopt and document the 1 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Approve the cap as the supported Browser CLI boundary and add the user-facing contract and focused boundary coverage before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The only concrete person identified for this exact changed surface is the contributor who authored the implementation; current-main ownership requires a maintainer-side history lookup.
